Convert OpenTelemetry GenAI spans

Source: R/otel-adapter.R
as_trajectory_otel.Rd

as_trajectory_otel() builds a TrajectoryBundle from OpenTelemetry spans that follow the GenAI semantic conventions, as emitted by ellmer and recorded by Posit Connect's content observability store or written to local OTLP files. Read those spans with read_connect_traces() or read_otel_traces().

Each conversation is reconstructed from its most recent chat span: provider instrumentation records the whole message history on every model call, so the last call carries the complete exchange. execute_tool spans contribute the timing and failure of each tool call, which the message history alone does not record.

A shinychat conversation-titling call (system instructions beginning "You title chat conversations.") is never chosen over another model call, even when it started last. Its usage stays in the conversation's totals in metadata$otel, and metadata$otel$title_calls reports how many title calls there were and their tokens.

When the chosen span records its output but omits gen_ai.input.messages, as ellmer does when a turn holds content it cannot serialize, the history is recovered from the latest earlier model call in the conversation that recorded its input, followed by the output of each later call. A span with neither attribute had message capture turned off and is left contentless. Messages that no span recorded are reported as capture$input or capture$tool_result losses, so assess_trajectory_scans() does not treat the transcript as complete.

Usage

as_trajectory_otel(
  x,
  trajectory_id = NULL,
  source_uri = NULL,
  metadata = list()
)

otel_group_conversations(spans)

Arguments

x

A list of conversations, as returned by read_connect_traces() or read_otel_traces(), or a flat list of spans to be grouped.

trajectory_id

Optional trajectory identifier. Must be NULL when x holds more than one conversation.

source_uri

Optional URI recording where the spans were read from.

metadata

Optional named list attached to every trajectory.

spans

A flat list of parsed spans.

Value

A TrajectoryBundle.

commons agents

commons wraps each turn in a commons_conversation_turn span and records each answer's provenance in a commons_provenance span. These spans are kept with their conversation, never counted against a reader's span budget, and never used as a transcript, so token totals, model calls, and resource measures are unchanged by them. Each exchange of the transcript becomes a "commons:provenance" event in the form as_trajectory_commons() gives: value holds provenance_tag and the full citation_decisions parsed from commons.citation.candidates (sanitized and bounded by the payload limit, with a loss when truncated), metadata$exchange_index numbers the exchange, and each turn's round_index is its exchange. As in commons, a user turn opens an exchange unless it returns tool results or is an internal reminder; reminder turns carry commons_internal = TRUE in their metadata. Unlike the commons reader, timestamp is the time the record's span ended. A record attaches to an exchange only when the history its turn recorded matches the transcript, and conflicting records for one exchange leave it unclassified with a loss. The Connect user commons records (commons.connect.user) is kept as metadata$otel$user. commons setup spans such as commons_agent_create belong to no conversation and are ignored.

Deputy agents

Deputy wraps each agent run in a deputy.run span. Like commons' spans it is kept with its conversation, never counted against a span budget, and never used as a transcript or a measure. A conversation's root runs, the turns of one chat, stay one trajectory. Each subagent run (one with deputy.parent.run.id) becomes its own trajectory, holding the model and tool calls under its run span, with the ID otel/<conversation>/<run ID> and parent_trajectory_id set when its parent run is in the same input. Otherwise the parent run ID stays in metadata with a parent_run_id loss. A model or tool call that no run's ancestry reaches stays with the lead and is reported with a deputy.run loss.

The latest run speaks for its trajectory. run_id is its deputy.run.id, and metadata carries session_id, agent_id, parent_run_id, delegation_id, stop_reason, and the ten-field ending described in as_trajectory_deputy(). The span records only the stop reason, the final finish reason, and whether the answer was cut off, so by, field, actual, limit, wrapped_up, and phase are NA. class is "RunEndingAnswered" or "RunEndingCutOff" for stop reason "complete", "RunEndingStopped" for any other reason Deputy exports by name except a limit or failure reason, and NA for those and for "custom", because a caller or hook can stop a run with a limit's or failure's own word. The trajectory status then follows the Deputy adapter's mapping from class, or from the stop reason when class is NA.

Deputy exports nine event types as span events, each with only identifiers and decisions. They become events named as the Deputy adapter names the same events, timestamped from the span event:

Span eventBundle eventNotes
deputy.permissiondeputy:permissioncall_id from tool_call_id; "failed" when decision is "deny"
deputy.structured_attemptdeputy:structured_attempt"failed" when valid is false; no attempted value
deputy.fallbackdeputy:fallbackfallback_index
deputy.compactiondeputy:compactionsuccessful compactions only
deputy.hookdeputy:hookhook, decision
deputy.file_checkpointdeputy:file_checkpointcheckpoint_id
deputy.delegationdeputy:delegationdelegation_id
deputy.warningdeputy:warningcode; no message
deputy.stopdeputy:stop

Other attributes stay in event metadata. Deputy does not export its other event types, so OTel bundles have no deputy:approval, deputy:limit_wrap_up, deputy:compaction_error, tool, request, or content events, and no tool names, inputs, results, or error messages. A run span's first 1,000 span events are read; a span with more is reported with a capture$events loss counting the events left out. Conversations without a deputy.run span are unaffected.

Spans are grouped into conversations by the gen_ai.conversation.id attribute, walking up the span's ancestry to find it. A conversation without that attribute anywhere in its ancestry falls back to its trace id, which groups a single model call rather than a session.

See also

read_connect_traces() to fetch spans from Posit Connect, and read_otel_traces() to read local trace files.
